gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states that a front-and-rear dash cam writes both cameras to one removable microSD card with no second copy, or that DDPAI's D²save design adds soldered eMMC memory beside the card.
standout_why: Compared against dashcamtalk.com, pcworld.com and knowledgelib.io (cited), plus productbible.com and truepicked.com (top results). Between them they already cover hardwire kits for parking mode, low-voltage cutoff and current draw (PCWorld), supercapacitor against battery (truepicked, productbible, dashcamtalk), the A229 Plus's 60 fps with HDR off or 30 fps with it on (productbible), the A810 Lite's drop to 24/25 fps in dual recording (knowledgelib, dashcamtalk), and high-endurance cards with monthly formatting (truepicked, knowledgelib). None mentions eMMC or a second copy of crash clips; PCWorld only notes that some cameras use internal storage, citing a Miofive. None states the rear-cable limit either. Two pages were not read: vortexradar.com (cited) returned HTTP 403 and thecargearguide.com failed on a certificate error. The rating stays at 2 because DDPAI's N5 Pro page was rate-limited (HTTP 429) today, so the failover wording for that exact model is not sourced; only the dual-storage design on DDPAI's sibling listings is.
decides: It does not overturn the VIOFO A229 Plus 2CH as the image-quality pick, but that pick fits the budget only at a retailer: viofo.com listed it at $229.99 on 2026-11-21, while ChatGPT's $159.99 was a Best Buy listing. The storage finding gives the DDPAI N5 Pro (our link) the segment 'crash clip survives a failed card', and it is the only under-$200 front-and-rear candidate here with built-in memory, per our record. Two things need checking before that row is used. First, DDPAI's store search returned $259.00 (compare-at $379.00) for 'N5 Pro' today against our record's $179.00 store price; I could not open the product page to see which variant that is. Second, the failover wording must be read from DDPAI's N5 Pro page or manual. Parking mode on every candidate needs a hardwire kit bought separately ($17.99 to $29.99 at the makers' stores today), which still leaves a $159.99 camera under $200 before a card.

findings.label: Why parking mode needs a constant feed, and what it draws (named reviewer)
findings.value: PCWorld: kits "connect the dash cam directly to a constant 12-volt source"; a dash cam "will only consume about 0.25 to 0.45 amps per hour"; low-voltage cutoff is "a safeguard against dead batteries"
findings.source_title: Best dash cams 2025: Reviews and buying advice | PCWorld
findings.note: A cited rival already has this, so it is not the gap. PCWorld sets the draw against a 45 Ah car battery and says a few days of parking would be needed to drain it noticeably.

findings.label: What the rival pages say about card failure and built-in memory

findings.source_title: Best Front and Rear Dash Cams (2026): 2-Channel Picks | Product Bible
